exercises.prompt: Implement average3(a, b, c) so it returns the average of the three numbers, rounded to the nearest whole number.
exercises.solution:
def average3(a, b, c):
    return round((a + b + c) / 3)
hints: An average is the sum of the values divided by how many there are — three here — and then rounded.
(a + b + c) / 3 gives the raw mean as a float; round(x) snaps it to the nearest whole number.
return round((a + b + c) / 3); the inner parentheses make the addition happen before the division.

exercises.prompt: Implement floor_divide(a, b) so it returns how many whole times b fits into a, discarding any remainder — integer division. For example floor_divide(7, 2) is 3. Assume a is zero or positive and b is a positive integer.
exercises.solution:
def floor_divide(a, b):
    return a // b
hints: Plain division with / gives a float (7 / 2 is 3.5); you want only the whole-number part.
Floor division // divides and rounds down to a whole number in one step: 7 // 2 is 3.

exercises.prompt: Implement is_even(n) so it returns True when the integer n is even and False when it is odd. Zero is even, and negative even numbers like -2 count as even too.
hints: A number is even exactly when dividing it by 2 leaves no remainder.
The remainder operator % gives that leftover: n % 2 is 0 for evens.
return n % 2 == 0 — this stays correct for 0 and for negatives.

exercises.prompt: Implement last_digit_of_power(base, exp) so it returns the last (units) digit of base raised to the exp power. Because 2 ** 10 is 1024, last_digit_of_power(2, 10) is 4. Assume base and exp are non-negative integers, and remember that any number to the 0 power is 1.
hints: Two steps: raise base to the exp power, then pull off the last digit of that result.
base ** exp computes the power; the last digit of a whole number is its remainder when divided by 10, i.e. % 10.

exercises.prompt: Implement abs_difference(a, b) so it returns the distance between the two numbers — how far apart they are — as a non-negative value. abs_difference(3, 5) and abs_difference(5, 3) are both 2.
exercises.solution:
def abs_difference(a, b):
    return abs(a - b)
hints: The distance between two numbers is their difference with any negative sign removed.
a - b might come out negative; abs(x) turns a negative into its positive twin and leaves positives unchanged.

exercises.prompt: Implement clamp_range(x, lo, hi) so it limits x to the range lo..hi, this time without any if — use min and max. Return lo when x is below lo, hi when x is above hi, and x otherwise. Assume lo <= hi.
exercises.solution:
def clamp_range(x, lo, hi):
    return max(lo, min(x, hi))
hints: Do it in two moves with no if: first stop x from going above hi, then stop that result from dropping below lo.
min(x, hi) caps the top; wrapping it in max(lo, ...) raises the floor.
